name: Luxardo Fernet Amaro
place: Torreglia, in the Euganean Hills near Padua, Veneto, Italy

facts.base: About 15 herbs, roots and spices, gentian, cardamom, liquorice and saffron among them, infused in alcohol
facts.cask: No cask or wood ageing is stated
facts.law: An Italian amaro in the fernet style, a bitter herbal liqueur; no appellation governs it

made: Luxardo makes it at Torreglia, in the Euganean Hills near Padua, where the family house has worked since 1947. About fifteen herbs, roots and spices, among them gentian, cardamom, liquorice and saffron, are infused in alcohol over a long maceration, and the liqueur is bottled dark at 40 per cent. The full recipe, made since 1889, stays the family's own, and no wood ageing is stated.
taste: Dark and bracing: liquorice, bitter gentian root and warm cardamom on the nose. The palate is dry and firmly bitter, with spice and a little saffron over a faint sweetness, and the finish is long, bitter and warming.

lines.s10: Luxardo Fernet Amaro is a dark, bitter Italian fernet from the maraschino house near Padua: herbs and roots, bottled at 40 per cent.
lines.s20: Luxardo Fernet Amaro is the bitter herbal digestivo of the Luxardo family, made since 1889 from about fifteen herbs, roots and spices, gentian, cardamom, liquorice and saffron among them. It is dark, dry and bracing, a fernet in the same style as Fernet-Branca.
lines.s45: This is Luxardo Fernet Amaro, from the Luxardo family, the maraschino house, who have made liqueurs since 1821 and work today at Torreglia, in the hills near Padua. About fifteen herbs, roots and spices, gentian, cardamom, liquorice and saffron among them, are infused in alcohol and bottled dark at 40 per cent. It is bracing and dry: liquorice and bitter roots, warm spice and a long, bitter, warming finish. We pour it neat at room temperature after dinner, or over one large cube, and it can stand in for Fernet-Branca in a Toronto. Luxardo has made its fernet since 1889.
lines.sale: Luxardo Fernet Amaro is a bitter after-dinner fernet from the maraschino house, dark, dry and full of herbs. Try it neat at room temperature, or stirred with rye in a Toronto.

serve.neat: Neat at room temperature, about an ounce, as a digestivo after dinner.
serve.rocks: Over one large cube, or long with cola, the way Argentina drinks fernet.
serve.glass: A small tulip or cordial glass neat; a rocks glass for the cube.
serve.classic: The Toronto, rye with fernet, sugar and bitters; also the Hanky Panky and the Fernet con Coca.

guest: Luxardo Fernet Amaro is an Italian bitter herbal liqueur, a fernet, from the family that makes maraschino: dark, dry and bracing, sipped neat after dinner.
story: Girolamo Luxardo, a Genoese who settled at Zara on the Dalmatian coast, founded the family distillery there in 1821 to make maraschino from the local marasca cherry, building on the cherry liqueur his wife, Maria Canevari, had made at home. Luxardo added its fernet in 1889. The Second World War left the Zara distillery in ruins, and in 1947 the family began again at Torreglia, in the Euganean Hills near Padua, where Luxardo still makes every bottle.
watch: Not Fernet-Branca: a guest or a recipe naming Branca means another house's fernet. Offer this as the same style, and say so.
It is bitter and strong: pour small measures, and warn a guest who expects a sweet liqueur.
A Luxardo on the dessert menu is Luxardo's cherries or maraschino, never this fernet: the same family, a different bottle.
asks: Turn the amaro at the left end of the liqueur shelf at lineup: confirm the label reads Luxardo Fernet Amaro in full, and how the bar pours it.

recall.prompt: What is Luxardo Fernet Amaro, and how is it poured?
recall.answer: A bitter Italian fernet from the Luxardo family at Torreglia, near Padua: about fifteen herbs, roots and spices, gentian, cardamom, liquorice and saffron among them, infused in alcohol and bottled at 40% ABV. Neat at room temperature after dinner, over a cube, or stirred in a Toronto.

quiz.q: In which year did the Luxardo house add its fernet to the range?
quiz.explain: The fernet dates from 1889. Luxardo was founded at Zara in 1821 and moved to Torreglia in 1947.

quiz.q: Where is Luxardo Fernet Amaro made today?
quiz.explain: Torreglia, in the Euganean Hills near Padua, since 1947. Zara was the first home, destroyed in the Second World War; Saronno is Lazzaroni's town.

quiz.q: Which classic stirs rye whiskey with fernet, sugar and bitters?
quiz.explain: The Toronto. The Hanky Panky uses fernet with gin and sweet vermouth; the Manhattan and Sazerac use no fernet.
